The drill now names the container it restored last.
config/list: Name of the server: the Linux host name and the name Windows shows under "Network" (\\<hostName>). At most 15 characters.
What kind of node this machine is. The base (adminuser, SSH, hs, health check, push messages) is on in every role. Needs a rebuild.
Identifier ZFS needs, 8 hex characters. Create it once and never change it:

Time zone of the server, e.g. "Europe/Vienna" (list: `timedatectl list-timezones`). It sets the clock the logs, the timers (backup at 04:00, ...) and the time on the Matrix cards use, and the TZ of the film apps. Default: UTC, which is why a card can be hours off. After changing it run `hs recipe matrix-hook` and the recipes of the film apps (radarr, sonarr, ...) again, so the containers pick it u
SSH public keys that may log in as adminuser, one per PC (the contents of each PC's ~/.ssh/<key>.pub). Manage them with `hs ssh-key`.

Optional parts of the server that are switched on, as a list of names (one folder each in capabilities/). Today: "metrics", and the extensions "games" and "posters" (`hs ext enable <name>` edits this list; a package without a Nix module needs no rebuild). A part whose old switch is set (for example metrics = true) counts as on even when it is not listed here. Otherwise needs a rebuild. docs/PLAN-m
Default language of the web interface: "en" or "de". The hs commands print English only. Default "en".
Keyboard layout of the console on the server itself (keyboard and screen), e.g. "de". Default: the US layout.
Icons in the interface (locks, marks, health):
Three status lines when you log in over SSH: problems, last backup, system disk. They come from files the timers keep, so they cost no time. `hs motd` shows them on demand. Default true.

Which version `hs update` follows: Beta and edge can break things. Changing it moves nothing by itself: it takes effect at the next `hs update`, which asks you to type the channel name when you switch to a newer one.

The web interface (browser): one service on this server, reachable from the home networks and Tailscale, never from the internet. Only members of Domain Admins can sign in, and the local adminuser (the only way in while the storage is locked). Plain HTTP, so keep it off networks you do not trust. Default false. Needs a rebuild. docs/PLAN-web-backend.md
The port of the web interface. Default 8480. Needs webUi = true.

Extra names the web interface answers to (the Host header), besides IP addresses, the server's own name, <name>.local, the Tailscale name and the gateway's local domain. Other names are refused (protection against DNS rebinding). Use it when the page is reached by another name, for example "nas.example.org,files.lan". "*" switches the check off. Default empty. No rebuild.

The domain group whose members sign in to the web interface as viewer (ADR 0012): they may look at everything that shows no secret. Domain Admins are admins. `hs group roles` creates the groups. Default "hn-viewers". No rebuild.

The domain group whose members sign in to the web interface as app manager (ADR 0012): they may also change instances and apps. Domain Admins are admins. `hs group roles` creates the groups. Default "hn-app-managers". No rebuild.
The main colour of the web interface, as #rrggbb. The lighter and darker tints are derived from it. Default "#9184d9" (purple). Medium-light colours read best on the dark ground.

HTTPS for the web interface through Tailscale (`tailscale serve`): the page then listens on this server only and is reached at https://<host>.<your-tailnet>.ts.net from devices in your tailnet; the home-network port is closed. Needs once: `sudo tailscale up` on the server and "HTTPS certificates" switched on in the Tailscale admin console (DNS). Default false. Needs webUi = true and a rebuild.

Also open the web interface on the home network, by the server's address (plain HTTP, for example http://10.10.10.95:8480), next to the https address of webTailscale. Default true. Without webTailscale it is the only address on the home network anyway. With webTailscale on and webLan off the page is reachable only through Tailscale.
The guides and the command reference as a page of the web interface ("Docs", the capability docs). Built by `hs docs build` (`hs update` does it). Default true. Needs webUi = true and a rebuild.

Run the test-lab on the branch develop every night (the capability testlab, off by default: it needs `testlab` in `capabilities`, KVM and Incus with nested virtualization, and it builds the installer ISO, so it is for a dedicated build server, never a normal install). The run is a job and a failure sends a push message. `hs testlab run` starts it by hand. Needs a rebuild. Not tested on hardware ye

A terminal in the web interface: a "Terminal" button in the top bar (a shell on this server, as adminuser, like an SSH login; root needs sudo and adminuser's password as always) and one on each instance (a shell inside it). Whoever may sign in to the web interface may open it, so switch it on only when you are fine with that. Sessions end after 30 minutes without typing and after 8 hours; nothing

How long an interactive app setup (hs sys recipes start ... --interactive, the web wizard) waits for the answer to a question, in hours. After that the run is cancelled cleanly and has to be started again. Default 24.

How long the browser terminal may stay without typing before the browser connection closes, in minutes (only typing counts, not output). The shell itself keeps running in tmux: sign in again and the terminal reattaches, so a long job (a big move between disks) survives. Default 30.
The longest a single browser terminal connection lasts, in hours; after that it closes and reattaches the same way. The web login itself still ends after 12 hours. Default 8.

EXPERIMENTAL and hidden, not tested on hardware: lets an app whose update policy is "automatic" update itself inside the quiet window (patch and minor releases of apps from the default repositories only). Off by default; nothing runs and "hs apps policy <app> automatic" is refused while it is false.
EXPERIMENTAL: the quiet window (local time, HH:MM-HH:MM, may pass midnight) in which automatic app updates may run. Only used when appsAutoupdateEnabled is true. Default "03:00-05:00".
The physical network card, check with `ip link`.
Subnets that may use the Samba shares, separated by spaces.

Tagged VLANs for the Incus containers and VMs. The key is the name (at most 12 characters; it becomes the bridge "br-<name>" and an Incus profile). Exactly one VLAN must have `default = true`: new instances land there. A second one looks like this:
Which addresses of the container network the router hands out by DHCP: the last number, from and to. Fixed addresses should lie outside. Default [100, 199].

The label in front of the domain for this server's local names: the gateway proxy gives services <service>.<siteName>.<domain> (one wildcard record *.<siteName>, made by a person). Lower case letters, digits and hyphens. Default: hostName.
The Incus web UI (https://<server>:8443/ui/) and the network address of the Incus API.

The internal link of Incus: a host-only network between the server (first address) and the cloudflared container (second address), no router involved. Change it only when the default overlaps a network you use; then run the cloudflared recipe again and change the tunnel's service address in Cloudflare. Needs hs rebuild.

The ISO library: the folder with the install images for virtual machines (hs iso, the Instances page). It can be a folder on a share or a bulk disk when the images are big. Images already in the old folder are not moved. Default "/var/lib/hs/iso".
SSH (port 22) over the server's IP address from the home networks.

Reach the home networks (admin pages, shares) from outside through Tailscale: this server becomes a subnet router. Default false. After `hs rebuild` run once: then approve the routes in the Tailscale admin console.

How the data disks under /bulk are organised. Default "zfs". Only without a pools line; with one, the kind is chosen per pool (hs pool <name> --kind). Disks are added with `hs manage-pool` in both cases, never listed here.
{ tank = { role = "data", kind = "zfs" }, ssd = { role = "apps", kind = "zfs" } }

The storage pools of this server: the key is the pool name (a lower case letter, then up to 11 letters or digits), `role` is "data" (shares) or "apps" (Incus storage, SSD shares), `kind` is "zfs" or "snapraid" (at most one). Without this line the two classic rows apply, derived from bulkType. `pools = {}` is a server without any pool: apps run on the system disk, no shares. The line is written by

The apps pool behind the Incus storage pool `default`, or "dir" for Incus' folder on the system disk. Written by hs pool when a second apps pool is added, never by hand. Without it: the first apps pool (or dir when there is none).

How often the SnapRAID parity is updated, in hours. Default 24 (once a night at 03:00, so the disks can sleep the rest of the day); allowed 1 2 3 4 6 8 12 24. It starts at 03:00, so 4 means 03:00 07:00 11:00 15:00 19:00 23:00. New and changed files are unprotected until the next run; a run only works on what changed, but each run wakes every disk. Only for bulkType = "snapraid".

Automatic ZFS snapshots of every share, hourly: the last 24 hours, 7 days and 4 weeks are kept. Default false. Only for bulkType = "zfs" (with "snapraid" the backup is the history). Snapshots hold deleted files, so they use space. Leave a share out with `hs share <share> auto off` (pelican-backups is out from the start). Get a file back with `hs share <share> snapshots`, then rollback.

Upper limit of the ZFS read cache (ARC) in GiB. Default 12; 0 means no limit. Without a limit ZFS takes nearly all of the RAM. The cache gives memory back when programs need it, so a limit only matters if you want that RAM for containers and VMs; a smaller cache means more reads from the disks. Applies after `hs rebuild` (the running value changes at once, a shrunk cache empties over time).

Let the spinning bulk, parity and backup disks go to sleep after this many minutes without access (hdparm -S). Default 0 = never. Saves power, noise and wear when the server is idle; SnapRAID setups gain most (only the disk with a file wakes). Costs 10 to 20 seconds on the first access after a sleep, and the disks of a mirror wake one after the other. SSDs, NVMe, the system disk and the `fast` poo

Sleep time per pool, in minutes, instead of `diskSpindownMinutes`: the key is a pool name (or `backup` for the backup disk), 0 = never. One value per pool, none per disk. A raidz pool wakes all its disks at once, a mirror one after the other, and hourly `shareSnapshots` on ZFS keeps the pool awake (`hs config check` warns about that pair). Applies after `hs rebuild`; `hs disk spindown status` show

Allow the file manager to copy, move and delete files. Test it in a VM first (docs/PLAN-storage-nas.md). false (default) browsing and plans only: `hs sys fm start` refuses copy, move, delete, rename and new folder true the file manager changes files This code has never run on real disks. Switch it on only after the VM test of the plan passed.
Has the first-run checklist been dealt with? The web interface shows its Setup page (and a reminder on the summary) until this is true. Set it by hand or with the button on the Setup page.
Does a share that appears later go into `hs backup` by itself? Shares that are in the backup when this becomes false stay in it.
Does a container that an app recipe sets up go into `hs backup` by itself? Containers that are in the backup stay in it.

The rotating off-site disk (label `backup-offsite`): after `hs backup offsite now` copied to it, the expiry entry `offline-backup-disk` moves to today plus this many days, and the health check warns before that date. Default 30.

The Active Directory domain this server joins as a file server; share logins and groups then come from the domain. `realm` is the domain, `workgroup` its short name. `hs recipe domain` sets this up. After the rebuild join once:

The login for SSH, sudo, the web interface (local sign-in) and the owner of every file on the shares. Chosen at install. Changing it on an installed server is not supported: the old account, its home and the owner of all share files would stay.

Push messages when a disk, a pool or a scheduled job has a problem. They are POSTed to this address, ntfy.sh style: pick a long random topic (whoever knows it can read along) and subscribe to it in the ntfy app. Use a service that does NOT run on this server (e.g. the public ntfy.sh): while the vault is closed every container is down. It also carries "unlock needed" (urgent), "started", "going dow

A "still alive" message to this address every 15 minutes (the health check). A watcher OUTSIDE this server (vps/hs-watch.sh on the VPS) raises the alarm when the messages stop: power cut, network down, crash, or the tunnel to the internet broken. Use a second long random topic, not the one of notifyUrl. Set up: docs/operations.md

A second push channel (ntfy style, like notifyUrl), for example a second topic that a bridge turns into a Matrix message. It only gets messages at or above notifySecondMinPriority, so it stays quiet unless something is wrong. The first channel is always tried first and a failure of one never stops the other.
The lowest priority that is also sent to notifyUrlSecond: min, low, default, high (default) or urgent.

Turns on the part "notifications" (channels, the Notifications page in the web interface) without a rebuild. An existing notifyUrl does the same by itself. The first-run checklist (Setup page) sets this. Default false.

Quiet hours for push messages (server time, may cross midnight). Messages below priority high (info, "all clear", started, updated) are held and sent as one message when the window ends; high and urgent messages (problems, alarms, "unlock needed") are always sent at once. The journal gets every message when it happens. Off by default.

Level 1 of the automatic reaction: when a disk fails its SMART check, a pool is degraded or a pool is above 95 % full or will be full within a week, the health check pauses the parity sync, the scrub and the cache mover and says so in its message. It never deletes, formats or moves anything. Off by default; lift a pause with: hs health resume.

Level 2 of the automatic reaction: when a pool is above 98 % full or will be full within a day, freeze the apps that write to it (Samba stays as it is) and say so in one message. Nothing is deleted. Off by default; let the apps run again with: hs storage incident resume

Level 3 of the automatic reaction: when a disk turns failing and the newest backup is older than 24 hours, start hs backup now (it only reads the pools and writes the backup disk). A copy from disk to disk is never automatic: the message names hs disk <disk> move. Off by default.

Hand out numbers about load, disks and pools and collect them with Prometheus ON THIS SERVER (127.0.0.1:9090 only), so the history has no gap while the storage is locked. `hs recipe monitoring` sets this itself and installs Grafana (and Loki) in a container that reads from it. Default false.
How many days Prometheus keeps its numbers. Default 30. Needs metrics = true.
The most disk space (GB, on the system disk) Prometheus may use; whichever limit is reached first wins. Default 5. Needs metrics = true.

One small read-only status document (http://<server>:9740/status.json: network counters, pools, disk health, backup age, problems) for a Stream Deck, a wall monitor or Home Assistant. Home networks and Tailscale only, no secrets in it. Default false. Needs a rebuild.

Where the web interface reads the status document of the proxyserver (the VPS): its deckApi address over Tailscale, http:// or https://. Only that one address is ever fetched. Default: off, the proxyserver pages then say "not configured". Needs webUi = true and a rebuild.

Where the web interface reaches the proxyserver (the VPS) to run `vps update` and `vps watch` for its buttons: the Tailscale name or address, for example "proxyserver" or "100.64.0.7". It logs in as root with a key of its own (`hs vps key` creates it and prints the line for the VPS's machine.nix: webKey) that can run update, watch and status there and nothing else. Default: off, the buttons stay g
Which router connection gives instances fixed addresses: the name of a provider in scripts/providers/network/. `hs net setup` sets it; setting it switches the capability network on. No rebuild.

Which page manages Docker, when the capability docker is on: webui (the web interface of hobnix, the default of `hs docker enable`; built later, until then it only records the choice), arcane, portainer, or none (Docker only). `hs docker enable` sets it; setting it switches the capability docker on. Only `hs docker disable` removes it. No rebuild.

Size of the docker container that `hs docker enable` creates: s = 2048 MiB and 2 CPUs, m = 4096 MiB and 4 CPUs, l = 8192 MiB and 8 CPUs. Read when `hs docker enable` runs; changing it later does not resize the container (use `hs ct docker set`, which the lock allows for ram and cpu). Default "m".
Advanced: memory of the docker container in MiB. 0 = from dockerSize. Read when `hs docker enable` runs; changing it later does not resize the container (use `hs ct docker set`).
Advanced: CPUs of the docker container. 0 = from dockerSize. Read when `hs docker enable` runs; changing it later does not resize the container (use `hs ct docker set`).

Which reverse proxy publishes the services of this server (hs services plan): the name of a provider in scripts/providers/reverse-proxy/. Setting it switches the capability reverse-proxy on. No rebuild. traefik-public = the gateway proxy also serves the public routes, through the tunnel and/or directly (direct mode; needs the capability gateway).
Which dashboard shows the services that want a tile (hs services): web = the page /dashboard of the web interface (needs webUi). Setting it switches the capability dashboard on. No rebuild.
The page /dashboard (variant web) may be opened without signing in, from the home network and Tailscale only. Off: it needs the sign-in of the web interface. Default false. No rebuild.
The domain names the reverse proxy serves, separated by commas, for example example.com,example.org. A service named "jellyfin" is wanted as jellyfin.<each domain>. No rebuild.

The public HTTPS port of the gateway proxy (extension passthrough: outside domains forwarded by SNI). 0 = off. Suggested 443: the router forwards the internet's 443 straight to the server. Another port (4443) only behind a router that translates ports. Never 80. Opens the port to the internet. Needs hs rebuild.

The public HTTP port of the gateway proxy (extension passthrough: outside domains forwarded by Host). 0 = off. Suggested 80: the router forwards the internet's 80 straight to the server; port 80 then also carries the local names, which refuse every source outside the home networks. Another port (8008) only behind a router that translates ports. Never 443. Opens the port to the internet. Needs hs r

What the gateway proxy does with a name it has no route for (asda.<site>.<realm>) when the request comes from a home network: "404" = Traefik's own 404 page, "drop" = close the connection where that is possible (the HTTPS entrypoints; plain HTTP answers 404 instead). The web interface answers only to <site>.<realm>. Needs hs rebuild.

What the gateway proxy does with a name it has no route for when the request comes from the internet (public ports): "drop" = close the connection on the public HTTPS port (plain HTTP answers 404), "404" = a 404 page; on the public HTTPS port "404" needs a certificate and is not accepted yet. Needs hs rebuild.
The port cloudflared sends the public traffic to (reverseProxy = traefik-public). 0 = off. Open only to gatewayTunnelFrom. Needs hs rebuild.
The addresses that may use gatewayTunnelPort. Empty (the default) = the cloudflared container on the internal link of Incus (10.99.0.2/32). Needs hs rebuild.

Let's Encrypt account address for the gateway's own certificates (direct mode: the router forwards 443 to this server with reverseProxy = traefik-public). Empty = off. Needs gatewayPublicHttps. Needs hs rebuild.
Use Let's Encrypt's test service first (certificates browsers do not trust, generous limits). Set false once hs gateway status shows a staging certificate for every host. Needs hs rebuild.

How the gateway asks Let's Encrypt for its own certificates (direct mode: gatewayAcmeEmail and gatewayPublicHttps set). "tls-alpn" (default) = TLS-ALPN-01 on port 443. "dns" = DNS-01 through the configured provider (Cloudflare only here). No HTTP-01. The value itself needs no rebuild; certificates are (re)requested at the next hs services apply / rebuild. Not tested on hardware yet.

The DNS provider for the ACME DNS-01 challenge (gatewayAcmeChallenge = "dns"). "cloudflare" reads the API token from a credential file (`hs gateway acme-token`, from stdin) and passes it to Traefik through systemd LoadCredential + CF_DNS_API_TOKEN_FILE (a path, never the token in the environment). Meaningless unless challenge = "dns". Not tested on hardware yet.

The domains served directly with own certificates (direct mode, needs gatewayAcmeEmail). Empty = none: every domain stays on the tunnel. Domains left out stay on the tunnel. No rebuild: hs services apply.

Graphics chip(s), for GPU use in containers (Jellyfin transcoding, Immich, ...): "nvidia", "amd" or "intel", or a list of them: ["nvidia", "intel"]. Without it no graphics driver is installed (a server without a card, a VM). Find out what is built in:

Which NVIDIA driver branch, only with gpu = "nvidia". "stable" (default) is the current driver for RTX 20xx cards and newer. A GTX 10xx (Pascal), GTX 9xx (Maxwell) or Titan V needs "legacy_580": the newest branch that still supports them ("Driver Not Loaded" in the log of nvidia-container-toolkit-cdi-generator is the sign of a card the driver does not support).

PCI devices that stay without a driver after every boot, listed by address (find it with `lspci`): hs-pci-bind attaches them early in the boot, before the pools are imported, and writes what the device looked like before and after to /var/lib/hs/pci-bind.log. For example the second chip of a 9300-16i SAS card. Default: none. Needs a rebuild.

Name of the Incus instance that is this server's domain controller. Only needed when it is neither "dc1" nor "dc2": hs finds those two by itself (dc1 first, a second server of a domain has dc2). Default: found automatically.

A UPS (battery backup) on this server, read through NUT: a clean shutdown when the battery is low or after `shutdownMinutes` on battery (0 = only when low), and push messages for power lost, power back and shutting down. Default off. Write just the driver as a string (`ups = "usbhid-ups"`) or a table; all keys are optional: `driver` (default usbhid-ups; find it with `nut-scanner -U`), `name` (defa

Disk the GRUB bootloader goes on, for a machine that does not boot with systemd-boot from an EFI partition (a VPS: BIOS or UEFI with GRUB, ESP at /boot). Default "" = systemd-boot, as on the home server.

SSH public keys of OTHER nodes that may ask this one for its status (`hs node status`). Each key gets the forced command scripts/node-remote.sh and nothing else (restrict): it runs the fixed words of that script, never a shell. On an edge node the keys belong to root (ssh port 2222, as `hs node add --kind vps` on the main node expects), otherwise to adminuser. `hs node key <name>` on the other nod

The mail domain this node is the MX for (the capability edge-mail). Mail for it is relayed to the mail server (edgeStalwartIp).

Edge node (a public VPS, role = edge)
Game ports that need only TCP (rare), on top of edgeGamePorts.

Public addresses the outside watcher must see answer (any answer but "none" or a 5xx counts). No admin pages here. The two push addresses (the home server's heartbeat topic to watch, and the topic to alarm on) are secrets: `hs config set heartbeatUrl ...` and `hs config set notifyUrl ...` (files in /var/lib/hs, never in the repository).
Edge node (a public VPS, role = edge)

File with a reusable Tailscale auth key (mode 0600), read once at the first start so a headless server joins the tailnet by itself. Create the key in the admin console; with tailscaleTags it carries the tag. Default "" = join by hand (`sudo tailscale up`).

Tailscale tags this node asks for when it joins (for example ["tag:vps"]); the ACL in the admin console decides what a tag may reach.
